questions.question: What does LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) do differently from full fine-tuning?
options: It updates every single parameter in the model, just like full fine-tuning
It freezes the original model weights entirely and trains a small set of additional matrices alongside targeted layers instead
It deletes most of the model's original parameters
It only works on models with fewer than 1 million parameters
questions.explanation: LoRA keeps the original weights frozen and unchanged, training only small additional matrices, which dramatically reduces the number of trainable parameters compared to updating the entire model.

questions.question: What does QLoRA add on top of standard LoRA?
options: Nothing — QLoRA and LoRA are identical
Quantization of the frozen base model weights (e.g. storing them in 4-bit instead of 16-bit), further reducing the VRAM needed to load the base model for fine-tuning
A requirement to use multiple GPUs simultaneously
Full fine-tuning of all original weights in addition to the LoRA matrices
questions.explanation: QLoRA combines LoRA's parameter-efficient training with quantizing the frozen base weights to a lower precision, further cutting memory requirements and enabling fine-tuning of large models on more modest hardware.

questions.question: A team proposes full fine-tuning of a 70-billion-parameter model for a narrow behavioral adjustment (customer service tone). Which question best evaluates this proposal?
options: Should we just approve the full fine-tuning budget without further discussion?
Have we considered LoRA or QLoRA instead, given the typical order-of-magnitude reduction in cost and hardware requirements for this kind of behavioral adaptation task?
Why do we need any fine-tuning at all for a tone adjustment?
Should we switch to prompting instead without evaluating fine-tuning approaches?
questions.explanation: For narrow behavioral/style adaptation tasks, LoRA/QLoRA typically capture most of the benefit of full fine-tuning at a small fraction of the cost, making it the natural first question before committing to a full fine-tuning budget.
